# Muse Code round 1d: references without hidden extras (blind rebuild 2026-10-30) — verifier PASS WITH ISSUES (forge-factory-r1c-2026-10-30); user yes + H1 = option A, 2026-10-30

Claude's blind rebuild (results/blind-rebuild-2026-10-30, cloud box + grader, 1e-6) passed 8/10. Two misses are factory bugs:
1. **F5-2 (and any reference using overlapping cuts on one axis):** the reference cuts the main bore as two overlapping
   coaxial cylinders (X -1..87.8 and -7..1). Merging them into one cylinder (the same solid) gives volume 35990.856 vs
   35990.680 and FAILs at 1e-6 (probe: results/probe-tight-2026-10-30). Verifier correction (N1): both are the SAME
   solid (precise BRepGProp volume 35987.005411 for both); the cause is the default Volume() noise, which the overlap's
   face structure triggers (F5 up to 6.1e-4, F9 2.7e-6; other families <= 2e-13). A text-faithful answer can fail. Fix: every hole/bore in every family is ONE cut of one primitive
   (no two coincident or overlapping same-radius coaxial cuts; no coincident faces between cutters).
2. **F10-1 (all F10):** the rim's inner cut runs from Z = 34.3 − 1 into the body, so it removes body material below the
   top face that the text never mentions (blind answer volume 33525.1 vs reference 33433.2). Fix: build the rim ring as
   its own ring (outer minus inner, Z 34.3 to 38.7) and fuse it; no cutter may remove material the text does not describe.
Rules: all in experiments/final/MUSE_SPEC.md "Rules". Do not edit checks.py; cloud_cq.py only as in H1 below.

## Build in this round ONLY (experiments/factory/)
- generator.py: fixes 1 and 2 in every family where they apply (search all 10 for overlapping coaxial cuts and for
  overshoot cutters that reach material outside the feature they cut). Seed, ids, numbers and texts stay the same
  unless a text must change to describe the part; report any text change.
- make_jobs.py self-check, new column CUTS: per job, no two cutter primitives in the reference share an axis and radius
  while overlapping (a static scan of the reference source is fine). Keep all other columns.
- Re-run make_jobs.py; report sha256s and whether texts or dev ids changed.
- **H2 (verifier):** TEXT=REF exempts only 0, ±1 and the `/2` of a printed diameter; any other integer or any arithmetic
  on printed values (e.g. `(5.9 + 1)` used as a size) is flagged unless it is an overshoot of a through-cut. Test: a
  reference box Y −3..3 against the text "5.9 wide" fails TEXT=REF.
- **H1 (user choice, filled in before launch):** **option A (user, 2026-10-30)**: the FACTORY grader in experiments/final/cloud_cq.py
  computes every volume used in the mismatch (answer XOR reference, and the reference volume it is divided by) with
  precise BRepGProp (eps 1e-9, e.g. `OCP.BRepGProp.BRepGProp.VolumeProperties_s(shape, props, 1e-9)`), tolerance unchanged
  (1e-6 tight, 0.2% verdict). The **first-test path stays byte-for-byte the same** (it calls checks.score as today):
  this is the only allowed edit to cloud_cq.py; checks.py stays frozen. Tests: F5's one-bore and two-bore solids give
  mismatch < 1e-9 in the factory path; a first-test grade gives the same result as before (fake shapes). Why: the
  default Volume() is noisy up to 6.1e-4 in F5 and 2.7e-6 in F9 (verifier H1), so correct answers failed.
- Tests: an overlapping-coaxial-cut reference fails CUTS; F10's reference does not cut below Z = 34.3 except the recess
  and bore (volume between Z 33.3 and 34.3 equals the text's body there).
## Done when
- pytest (same 5 folders) passes; make_jobs SELF-CHECK OK with TEXT=REF and CUTS 20/20 in all families.
Report: files changed, pytest line, table, sha256s, text changes, anything not followed.

Read text file `experiments/final/MUSE_SPEC.md`.
1|# Muse Code spec: cloud CadQuery box, factory, trained arm, final comparison (DRAFT)
2|
3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29. Needs the verifier's check and the user's yes before Muse Code runs.
4|Plan: experiments/final/PLAN.md. Factory details: experiments/factory/SPEC.md (binding, with the changes in §2 here).
5|
6|## Rules
7|- Work in ~/projects/forge. New files only in experiments/final/, experiments/factory/ and deploy/modal_forge.py; the
8|  one allowed edit outside them is §5 (runner_fc.py cached tokens) and §4's guard hook in experiments/train/forge_train.py.
9|- Do not edit frozen files: experiments/first-test/*, experiments/b2-hint/*, experiments/bmax/*, deploy/modal_glimmer.py,
10|  experiments/thinking/*. Import from them instead.
11|- Never open blind/ or experiments/option-a/; never print any expected*.json; code may use expected.json only inside
12|  the grader image.
13|- No network, no Modal runs, no model calls, no commit, never print keys. Tests are offline; any test that could reach
14|  Modal monkeypatches it to raise.
15|- Why the cloud: user rule "the Mac is the office": no AI-written answer code runs on the Mac.
16|
17|## 1. `experiments/final/cloud_cq.py`: cloud CadQuery box + grader
18|Same design as experiments/freecad/cloud_exec.py and cloud_grade.py (read both):
19|- Box: a fresh Modal Sandbox per answer (block_network=True, no secrets, no volumes, cpu 1, memory 1024-4096 MiB,
20|  90 s box, 60 s run = runner.RUN_TIMEOUT). Image: python:3.12-slim + the libGL apt line + `cadquery==2.8.0 cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1` (the
21|  Mac's versions; the grader pins the same) + a small run script. It holds no references, jobs or expected files.
22|- The run script executes answer.py, takes the `result` variable (same rule as runner.run_code: Workplane → its
23|  solid), and writes the part as **BREP** (exact; not STEP) plus a run-error text if it failed.
24|- Grader: a Modal function (app `forge-cq-grader`, cpu 1) with CadQuery 2.8 and checks.py baked in, plus
25|  /grader/first-test/{jobs.py, expected.json} and /grader/factory/jobs.jsonl. `grade(exam, job_id, brep_bytes)` →
26|  {verdict (0.2%, checks.TOL_DIFF), tight (1e-6), fails, measurements}. For first-test it scores against expected.json
27|  exactly as runner.py does; for factory it builds the job's reference program in the grader and scores both ways.
28|- `--check-refs --exam first-test|factory`: each reference built in the box → BREP → grader must PASS at 1e-6.
29|  Prints `REFS n/n PASS`.
30|- `--regrade <baseline results dir>`: re-run each recorded answer's code (from calls.jsonl) in the box, grade it, and
31|  write regrade.json with old verdict, new verdict (0.2%) and new tight (1e-6), per answer (the 199 final
32|  answers: BR 30, B2 90, BX 79), plus a measure-equality column: box measurements vs the recorded ones at the
33|  recorded print precision; print `MEASURE same=X changed=Y`; print `REGRADE same=X changed=Y`. (PLAN step 1.)
34|- Tests: BREP round trip of a simple part keeps volume and bbox at 1e-9; a fake sandbox returns bytes → grader
35|  verdict path; image file list has no references; regrade counts with fake records.
36|
37|## 2. Factory (experiments/factory/SPEC.md, build it, with these changes)
38|- Teacher answers run in cloud_cq's box and are graded by its grader at 1e-6 (not runner.run_code on the Mac).
39|- Reference programs and the generator's own self-checks (valid solids, wrong variants fail) are trusted generator
40|  code and may run locally in tests.
41|- cached tokens: read `usage["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"]` when present, else `usage["cached_tokens"]`,
42|  else 0. Test with the real Baseten usage shape (numbers illustrative):
43|  `{"prompt_tokens": 8307, "completion_tokens": 3438, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 7552}}`.
44|- `make_jobs.py` also writes the 20 dev jobs as a jobs file usable by §3 (`--jobs-file`).
45|
46|## 3. `experiments/final/runner_final.py`: the trained arm FT on the same yardstick
47|- Import from experiments/first-test/runner.py (frozen, unchanged): SYSTEM_PROMPT, build_messages, build_body,
48|  the code extraction, the summary/statistics helpers. Arm FT = arm A's messages (system + job text, no manual, no
49|  hint) and arm A's body (max_tokens 16000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64), with model "forge".
50|  Test: FT's messages and body equal runner.build_messages("A", …) / build_body(…) except the model name.
51|- Endpoint from env FORGE_URL / FORGE_KEY (missing → exit 2 with the variable name, no network).
52|- `--jobs dry|main` (first-test levels, as runner.py) or `--jobs-file <factory dev file>`; `--k`, `--workers 8`,
53|  `--budget`, `--gpu-start`, `--out`.
54|- Each answer: extract code → cloud box → cloud grader. calls.jsonl per answer (append live under a lock): job, rep,
55|  level, verdict (0.2%), tight (1e-6), fails, usage (prompt, completion, reasoning length), t_call_s, finish_reason.
56|- summary.json + report.md: pass rate all/medium/hard at 0.2% (decision) and at 1e-6 (reference), pass@k, tokens per
57|  correct part, seconds per answer (median, mean), arm wall-clock, $ per correct part = wall-clock h × $2.50 ÷ PASS.
58|- Budget guard as runner_fc (money left = cap − GPU time since gpu-start × $2.50/h; stop new calls when ≤ reserve).
59|
60|## 3b. Arm BX on the cloud box, only for missing answers (user: "finish until the 30 jobs")
61|- `runner_final.py --arms BX --fill-missing results/bmax-baseline-2026-10-29/main-B2BX`: run only the (job, rep)
62|  pairs with no BX final record (expected: H12 ×2, H13-H15 ×3 = 11), endpoint GLIMMER_URL/GLIMMER_KEY (base Glimmer).
63|- Same loop as the frozen runner.do_bx_call: import build_messages("BX", …), build_bx_body, bx_self_check_message,
64|  BX_MAX_CALLS, BX_ERROR_HEAD, the examples and hint from the frozen files. The only change: each program runs in the
65|  cloud box, which returns (run_error, measure) in the same measure format as run_code_sandboxed (xmin…zmax, volume,
66|  solids), and the verdict comes from the cloud grader. Write per-round + final records like run_suite does.
67|- Test: with fake model replies and a fake executor, the cloud BX loop sends exactly the same message list, round by
68|  round, as runner.do_bx_call does with the same fake executor (build, run error, self-check, no-code-block end).
69|- Default `--workers 12` for `--fill-missing` (one wave). If fewer final records than missing pairs exist at the end,
70|  exit 3 with "INCOMPLETE: ask the user" and write no summary that compare.py would accept.
71|- Log the vLLM image digest (from the server) into summary.json for every session.
72|- compare.py merges these records with the baseline BX records (no (job, rep) twice; refuses on a duplicate).
73|
74|## 4. Exam guard on the cloud box
75|forge_train.py's code check (run_train_code / default_train_meas) gets a hook to use cloud_cq's box for the training
76|record's code (measurements back from the grader-side measure of the BREP). The local sandbox path is removed for
77|training records. Exam references are still built in-process (trusted jobs.py). Test with a fake box.
78|
79|## 5. C1 fix in experiments/freecad/runner_fc.py
80|`cached_tokens_of` reads the nested Baseten field first (same rule as §2). Test with the real usage shape above.
81|
82|## 6. `deploy/modal_forge.py`: serve the trained model
83|Copy of deploy/modal_glimmer.py's settings (A100-80GB, same vLLM image and flags, max-model-len 32768, max_containers
84|1, 5-min scale-down, secret forge-glimmer) except: app `forge-trained`, model path `/vol/<name>/merged` from the
85|`forge-lora` volume (name from env FORGE_MODEL_NAME, default `final`), served name `forge`.
86|And `experiments/final/run_final_session.sh`: same behaviour as experiments/freecad/run_fc_session.sh (deploy, wait
87|ready, optional pilot + GO/STOP, whole-session cap with reserve, trap that always stops the app and prints it), for
88|runner_final.py with app forge-trained.
89|
90|## 7. `experiments/final/compare.py`: the pre-registered decision (PLAN step 6)
91|Inputs: FT's run dir and the baseline dirs results/bmax-baseline-2026-10-29/main-B2BX and main-BR. Paired bootstrap
92|over the 30 jobs (10,000 resamples, seed 20261029), per-job pass rate over that arm's answers (BX uses the answers it
93|has). If any of the 30 jobs still has no BX answer, compare.py refuses (exit 2) and names the jobs. Tokens per correct part are printed
94|split into prompt and completion; bar (d) prints wall-clock and $ per correct part first. Prints each bar (a)-(d) with the numbers and PASS/FAIL, then "CLAIM HOLDS" only if all four pass. Tables for
95|all/medium/hard. Tests: fake records for each bar at its boundary (−5, −15, 1.5×, ÷3) and one all-pass case, and the refusal
96|when a job has no BX answer.
97|
98|## Done when
99|- `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/factory experiments/freecad
100|  experiments/train experiments/common` passes (the old 150 plus the new tests).
101|- `runner_final.py --jobs main --out X` with no keys exits 2 with the missing-variable message, no network.
102|- `forge_train.py smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` still prints CAP REFUSED and exits 2.
103|Report: files changed, the pytest line, anything not followed.

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""Write the factory jobs file + dev split, with the self-checks.
3|
4|Writes experiments/factory/jobs.jsonl (200 jobs: id, family, text,
5|reference source), split.json (the 20 seed-chosen dev ids) and
6|jobs_dev.jsonl (the 20 dev jobs as a jobs file for the final-exam
7|runner's --jobs-file).
8|
9|Self-check (SPEC section 1): every reference builds one valid solid
10|in-process (trusted generator code); two "wrong" variants per family
11|(a moved feature, a wrong size) FAIL at 1e-6; no job text has difflib
12|ratio >= 0.9 (exact numbers) to any first-test job text; TEXT=REF: for
13|every job, the numbers in the text are re-parsed and each number the
14|reference program uses (its literal numbers, after rounding) must
15|appear in the text (a family passes only at 20/20). Prints a
16|10-family table.
17|"""
18|
19|import difflib
20|import json
21|import os
22|import re
23|import sys
24|
25|HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
26|if HERE not in sys.path:
27|    sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
28|
29|import generator
30|
31|JOBS_NAME = "jobs.jsonl"
32|SPLIT_NAME = "split.json"
33|DEV_JOBS_NAME = "jobs_dev.jsonl"
34|OVERLAP_LIMIT = 0.9
35|
36|NUM_RE = re.compile(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
37|# Whole-number construction constants (overshoot +-1, the origin, small
38|# counts) carry no design value and are exempt from the TEXT=REF check.
39|SMALL_INT = 8
40|
41|
42|def body_of(reference):
43|    """The reference program without the shared preamble helpers."""
44|    if reference.startswith(generator.PREAMBLE):
45|        return reference[len(generator.PREAMBLE):]
46|    return reference
47|
48|
49|def text_ref_ok(text, reference):
50|    """True when every design number the reference program uses appears
51|    in the job text (TEXT=REF).
52|
53|    Each numeric literal in the reference body (after rounding) must
54|    match a number parsed from the text within 1e-9, except whole-number
55|    construction constants with abs(v) <= 8. A text that prints 21.2
56|    while its reference uses 21.3 fails. (--check-refs grades a
57|    reference against itself and cannot see this.)
58|    Returns (ok, missing_literal_or_None)."""
59|    texts = [float(m) for m in NUM_RE.findall(text or "")]
60|    for m in NUM_RE.findall(body_of(reference or "")):
61|        v = float(m)
62|        if v == int(v) and abs(int(v)) <= SMALL_INT:
63|            continue
64|        if not any(abs(v - t) <= 1e-9 for t in texts):
65|            return False, m
66|    return True, None
67|
68|
69|def exam_texts():
70|    """First-test job texts (for the overlap self-check)."""
71|    import importlib.util as _ilu
72|
73|    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "first-test", "jobs.py")
74|    spec = _ilu.spec_from_file_location("factory_exam_jobs", path)
75|    mod = _ilu.module_from_spec(spec)
76|    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
77|    return [j["text"] for j in mod.JOBS]
78|
79|
80|def max_overlap(text, texts):
81|    """Largest difflib ratio of a job text to any exam text."""
82|    return max(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, text, e).ratio()
83|               for e in texts)
84|
85|
86|def self_check(jobs, texts):
87|    """Full self-check. Returns per-family rows:
88|    (family, name, n_valid, n_jobs, wrong_results, max_ratio, n_text_ref).
89|    n_text_ref is the TEXT=REF count: jobs whose every reference number
90|    (after rounding) appears in the text."""
91|    rows = []
92|    for family in range(1, generator.N_FAMILIES + 1):
93|        fam = generator.FAMILIES[family]
94|        sub = [j for j in jobs if j["family"] == family]
95|        n_valid = 0
96|        for job in sub:
97|            shape = generator.build_source(job["reference"])
98|            n_solids, valid = generator.shape_info(shape)
99|            if n_solids == 1 and valid:
100|                n_valid += 1
101|            else:
102|                print("INVALID REF %s: solids=%s valid=%s"
103|                      % (job["id"], n_solids, valid))
104|        ref = generator.build_source(sub[0]["reference"])
105|        wrongs = []
106|        for override in fam["wrong"](generator.first_params(family)):
107|            wsrc = fam["src"](override)
108|            passed, fails = generator.score_at_tight(wsrc, ref)
109|            wrongs.append((passed, fails))
110|        ratio = max(max_overlap(j["text"], texts) for j in sub)
111|        n_text_ref = 0
112|        for job in sub:
113|            ok, missing = text_ref_ok(job["text"], job["reference"])
114|            if ok:
115|                n_text_ref += 1
116|            else:
117|                print("TEXT!=REF %s: reference uses %s, not in the text"
118|                      % (job["id"], missing))
119|        rows.append((family, fam["name"], n_valid, len(sub), wrongs,
120|                     ratio, n_text_ref))
121|    return rows
122|
123|
124|def print_table(rows):
125|    """Print the 10-family self-check table."""
126|    print("%-28s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s" % (
127|        "FAMILY", "VALID", "WRONG-1", "WRONG-2", "OVERLAP", "TEXT=REF"))
128|    ok = True
129|    for family, name, n_valid, n_jobs, wrongs, ratio, n_text_ref in rows:
130|        cells = []
131|        v_ok = n_valid == n_jobs
132|        cells.append("%d/%d" % (n_valid, n_jobs))
133|        for passed, _fails in wrongs:
134|            cells.append("FAIL" if not passed else "PASS-BAD")
135|        cells.append("%.3f" % ratio)
136|        cells.append("%d/%d" % (n_text_ref, n_jobs))
137|        if not v_ok or any(p for p, _f in wrongs) \
138|                or ratio >= OVERLAP_LIMIT or n_text_ref != n_jobs:
139|            ok = False
140|        print("%-28s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s" % (
141|            "%d %s" % (family, name), cells[0], cells[1], cells[2],
142|            cells[3], cells[4]))
143|    print("SELF-CHECK %s" % ("OK" if ok else "FAIL"))
144|    return ok
145|
146|
147|def main(argv=None):
148|    import argparse as _ap
149|
150|    parser = _ap.ArgumentParser(description="Write factory jobs + split.")
151|    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default=HERE)
152|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
153|    jobs = generator.generate_all()
154|    dev_ids = generator.choose_dev_ids(jobs)
155|    dev_set = set(dev_ids)
156|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, JOBS_NAME), "w",
157|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
158|        for job in jobs:
159|            f.write(json.dumps(job) + "\n")
160|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, SPLIT_NAME), "w",
161|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
162|        json.dump({"seed": generator.SEED, "dev": dev_ids}, f, indent=1)
163|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, DEV_JOBS_NAME), "w",
164|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
165|        for job in jobs:
166|            if job["id"] in dev_set:
167|                f.write(json.dumps(job) + "\n")
168|    print("wrote %d jobs, %d dev ids" % (len(jobs), len(dev_ids)))
169|    rows = self_check(jobs, exam_texts())
170|    ok = print_table(rows)
171|    return 0 if ok else 1
172|
173|
174|if __name__ == "__main__":
175|    sys.exit(main())

1|"""Cloud CadQuery box + grader (MUSE_SPEC section 1).
2|
3|Why this file exists (user decision 2026-10-29): nothing a model writes
4|may run on the Mac. Every answer runs in a fresh Modal Sandbox
5|(block_network=True, no secrets, no volumes, cpu 1, memory 1024-4096
6|MiB, 90 s box); one sandbox per answer, terminated after use.
7|
8|Image: python:3.12-slim + the libGL apt line + ``cadquery==2.8.0
9|cadquery-ocp==7.9.3.1`` (the Mac's versions; the grader pins the same)
10|+ run_cq_box.py. It holds no references, jobs or expected files.
11|
12|Flow: write answer.py with sb.filesystem.write_text, run
13|``python /work/run_cq_box.py /work`` with sb.exec (60 s inside the 90 s
14|box, the baseline's speed limit), read back /work/answer.brep (bytes) +
15|/work/measure.json, then sb.terminate(). The run script takes the
16|``result`` variable (same rule as runner.run_code: Workplane gives its
17|solid) and writes the part as BREP (exact; not STEP). BREP answers over
18|20 MB are refused. The verdict and failure tags come only from the
19|grader; measure.json is for logs (the box runs untrusted code and must
20|not score itself).
21|
22|Grader: a Modal function (app ``forge-cq-grader``, cpu 1) with CadQuery
23|2.8 and checks.py baked in, plus /grader/first-test/{jobs.py,
24|expected.json} and /grader/factory/jobs.jsonl. ``grade(exam, job_id,
25|brep_bytes)`` scores first-test against expected.json exactly as
26|runner.py does; for factory it builds the job's reference program in
27|the grader and scores both ways (0.2% verdict + 1e-6 tight).
28|
29|Modal is imported lazily so the config helpers (sandbox kwargs, image
30|file list) are unit-testable offline. Tests inject a fake sandbox; any
31|test that could reach a real Modal call monkeypatches it to raise.
32|"""

164|def run_answer_in_box(answer_code, sandbox=None, sandbox_factory=None):
165|    """Run one answer string in the box. Returns {"brep_bytes",
166|    "measure", "log", "run_error"}; measure is logs-only, the grader
167|    decides.

170|    no args) is injected in tests; without either, a real Modal sandbox
171|    is created. BREP output over 20 MB raises ValueError. When the answer
172|    writes no BREP (run_cq_box exits 2 with its ERROR line on stderr),
173|    nothing raises: brep_bytes/measure come back None and run_error holds

226|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):
227|    """PASS iff every check holds and the mismatch fraction is within tol.
228|
229|    `check_fails`: failed checks at the baseline yardstick (bbox, volume,
230|    ...); `mismatch`: answer-XOR-reference fraction of reference volume
231|    (None when the shape could not be intersected). Returns
232|    (passed, fails).
233|    """
234|    fails = list(check_fails or [])
235|    if mismatch is None:
236|        fails = fails + ["mismatch error"]
237|    elif mismatch > tol:
238|        fails = fails + ["mismatch %.1f%%" % (100.0 * mismatch)]
239|    return (not fails), fails

242|def grade_result(check_fails, mismatch, measurements):
243|    """Grade one imported BREP: verdict at 0.2% + the 1e-6 recording.
244|
245|    Returns {"verdict", "tight", "fails", "fails_tight", "measurements"}.
246|    Pure (no cadquery): the Modal function supplies check_fails and the
247|    mismatch fraction from checks.score; tests pass synthetic values.
248|    """
249|    passed, fails = combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, TOL_VERDICT)

251|                                               TOL_TIGHT)

254|        "tight": "PASS" if passed_tight else "FAIL",
255|        "fails": fails,

257|        "measurements": measurements,

272|        _sys.path.insert(0, FIRST_TEST_DIR)
273|    import checks as _checks

278|        passed, fails, m = _checks.score(answer_shape, ref_shape, expected)
279|        d = m.get("mismatch")

282|                                              expected)
283|    finally:
284|        _checks.TOL_DIFF = old

290|    # pure combiner above only mirrors them for synthetic inputs).
291|    out["verdict"] = "PASS" if passed else "FAIL"
292|    out["tight"] = "PASS" if passed_t else "FAIL"
293|    out["fails"] = list(fails)
294|    out["fails_tight"] = list(fails_t)
295|    return out

302|    as answers: Workplane gives its solid). Needs cadquery.
303|    """
304|    import cadquery as _cq

310|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, _cq.Shape)]
311|        if len(vals) == 1:
312|            return vals[0]
313|        return _cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
314|    if isinstance(result, _cq.Assembly):
315|        return result.toCompound()

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""Write the factory jobs file + dev split, with the self-checks.
3|
4|Writes experiments/factory/jobs.jsonl (200 jobs: id, family, text,
5|reference source), split.json (the 20 seed-chosen dev ids) and
6|jobs_dev.jsonl (the 20 dev jobs as a jobs file for the final-exam
7|runner's --jobs-file).
8|
9|Self-check (SPEC section 1): every reference builds one valid solid
10|in-process (trusted generator code); two "wrong" variants per family
11|(a moved feature, a wrong size) FAIL at 1e-6; no job text has difflib
12|ratio >= 0.9 (exact numbers) to any first-test job text; TEXT=REF: for
13|every job, the numbers in the text are re-parsed and each number the
14|reference program uses (its literal numbers, after rounding) must
15|appear in the text (a family passes only at 20/20). Prints a
16|10-family table.
17|"""
18|
19|import difflib
20|import json
21|import os
22|import re
23|import sys
24|
25|HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
26|if HERE not in sys.path:
27|    sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
28|
29|import generator
30|
31|JOBS_NAME = "jobs.jsonl"
32|SPLIT_NAME = "split.json"
33|DEV_JOBS_NAME = "jobs_dev.jsonl"
34|OVERLAP_LIMIT = 0.9
35|
36|NUM_RE = re.compile(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
37|# Whole-number construction constants (overshoot +-1, the origin, small
38|# counts) carry no design value and are exempt from the TEXT=REF check.
39|SMALL_INT = 8
40|
41|
42|def body_of(reference):
43|    """The reference program without the shared preamble helpers."""
44|    if reference.startswith(generator.PREAMBLE):
45|        return reference[len(generator.PREAMBLE):]
46|    return reference
47|
48|
49|def text_ref_ok(text, reference):
50|    """True when every design number the reference program uses appears
51|    in the job text (TEXT=REF).
52|
53|    Each numeric literal in the reference body (after rounding) must
54|    match a number parsed from the text within 1e-9, except whole-number
55|    construction constants with abs(v) <= 8. A text that prints 21.2
56|    while its reference uses 21.3 fails. (--check-refs grades a
57|    reference against itself and cannot see this.)
58|    Returns (ok, missing_literal_or_None)."""
59|    texts = [float(m) for m in NUM_RE.findall(text or "")]
60|    for m in NUM_RE.findall(body_of(reference or "")):
61|        v = float(m)
62|        if v == int(v) and abs(int(v)) <= SMALL_INT:
63|            continue
64|        if not any(abs(v - t) <= 1e-9 for t in texts):
65|            return False, m
66|    return True, None
67|
68|
69|def exam_texts():
70|    """First-test job texts (for the overlap self-check)."""
71|    import importlib.util as _ilu
72|
73|    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "first-test", "jobs.py")
74|    spec = _ilu.spec_from_file_location("factory_exam_jobs", path)
75|    mod = _ilu.module_from_spec(spec)
76|    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
77|    return [j["text"] for j in mod.JOBS]
78|
79|
80|def max_overlap(text, texts):
81|    """Largest difflib ratio of a job text to any exam text."""
82|    return max(difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, text, e).ratio()
83|               for e in texts)
84|
85|
86|def self_check(jobs, texts):
87|    """Full self-check. Returns per-family rows:
88|    (family, name, n_valid, n_jobs, wrong_results, max_ratio, n_text_ref).
89|    n_text_ref is the TEXT=REF count: jobs whose every reference number
90|    (after rounding) appears in the text."""
91|    rows = []
92|    for family in range(1, generator.N_FAMILIES + 1):
93|        fam = generator.FAMILIES[family]
94|        sub = [j for j in jobs if j["family"] == family]
95|        n_valid = 0
96|        for job in sub:
97|            shape = generator.build_source(job["reference"])
98|            n_solids, valid = generator.shape_info(shape)
99|            if n_solids == 1 and valid:
100|                n_valid += 1
101|            else:
102|                print("INVALID REF %s: solids=%s valid=%s"
103|                      % (job["id"], n_solids, valid))
104|        ref = generator.build_source(sub[0]["reference"])
105|        wrongs = []
106|        for override in fam["wrong"](generator.first_params(family)):
107|            wsrc = fam["src"](override)
108|            passed, fails = generator.score_at_tight(wsrc, ref)
109|            wrongs.append((passed, fails))
110|        ratio = max(max_overlap(j["text"], texts) for j in sub)
111|        n_text_ref = 0
112|        for job in sub:
113|            ok, missing = text_ref_ok(job["text"], job["reference"])
114|            if ok:
115|                n_text_ref += 1
116|            else:
117|                print("TEXT!=REF %s: reference uses %s, not in the text"
118|                      % (job["id"], missing))
119|        rows.append((family, fam["name"], n_valid, len(sub), wrongs,
120|                     ratio, n_text_ref))
121|    return rows
122|
123|
124|def print_table(rows):
125|    """Print the 10-family self-check table."""
126|    print("%-28s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s" % (
127|        "FAMILY", "VALID", "WRONG-1", "WRONG-2", "OVERLAP", "TEXT=REF"))
128|    ok = True
129|    for family, name, n_valid, n_jobs, wrongs, ratio, n_text_ref in rows:
130|        cells = []
131|        v_ok = n_valid == n_jobs
132|        cells.append("%d/%d" % (n_valid, n_jobs))
133|        for passed, _fails in wrongs:
134|            cells.append("FAIL" if not passed else "PASS-BAD")
135|        cells.append("%.3f" % ratio)
136|        cells.append("%d/%d" % (n_text_ref, n_jobs))
137|        if not v_ok or any(p for p, _f in wrongs) \
138|                or ratio >= OVERLAP_LIMIT or n_text_ref != n_jobs:
139|            ok = False
140|        print("%-28s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s" % (
141|            "%d %s" % (family, name), cells[0], cells[1], cells[2],
142|            cells[3], cells[4]))
143|    print("SELF-CHECK %s" % ("OK" if ok else "FAIL"))
144|    return ok

146|
147|def main(argv=None):
148|    import argparse as _ap
149|
150|    parser = _ap.ArgumentParser(description="Write factory jobs + split.")
151|    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default=HERE)
152|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
153|    jobs = generator.generate_all()
154|    dev_ids = generator.choose_dev_ids(jobs)
155|    dev_set = set(dev_ids)
156|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, JOBS_NAME), "w",
157|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
158|        for job in jobs:
159|            f.write(json.dumps(job) + "\n")
160|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, SPLIT_NAME), "w",
161|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
162|        json.dump({"seed": generator.SEED, "dev": dev_ids}, f, indent=1)
163|    with open(os.path.join(args.out_dir, DEV_JOBS_NAME), "w",
164|              encoding="utf-8") as f:
165|        for job in jobs:

167|                f.write(json.dumps(job) + "\n")
168|    print("wrote %d jobs, %d dev ids" % (len(jobs), len(dev_ids)))
169|    rows = self_check(jobs, exam_texts())
170|    ok = print_table(rows)
171|    return 0 if ok else 1
172|
173|

175|    sys.exit(main())

164|def run_answer_in_box(answer_code, sandbox=None, sandbox_factory=None):
165|    """Run one answer string in the box. Returns {"brep_bytes",
166|    "measure", "log", "run_error"}; measure is logs-only, the grader
167|    decides.
168|
169|    `sandbox` (a live or fake sandbox) or `sandbox_factory` (called with
170|    no args) is injected in tests; without either, a real Modal sandbox
171|    is created. BREP output over 20 MB raises ValueError. When the answer
172|    writes no BREP (run_cq_box exits 2 with its ERROR line on stderr),
173|    nothing raises: brep_bytes/measure come back None and run_error holds
174|    run_cq_box's stderr (its ERROR line), for the runner's run_error.
175|    """
176|    own = False
177|    if sandbox is None:
178|        if sandbox_factory is not None:
179|            sandbox = sandbox_factory()
180|        else:
181|            sandbox = build_sandbox()
182|        own = True
183|    try:
184|        # Modal 1.6.3 is write_text(data, remote_path): keywords, so a
185|        # reordered fake or SDK signature cannot silently swap the args.
186|        sandbox.filesystem.write_text(
187|            data=answer_code or "",
188|            remote_path=WORK_DIR + "/" + ANSWER_NAME)
189|        proc = sandbox.exec(
190|            "python", RUN_PATH, WORK_DIR,
191|            env={"CQ_SCRATCH": WORK_DIR},
192|            timeout=EXEC_TIMEOUT_S,
193|        )
194|        log = _read_stream(getattr(proc, "stdout", None))
195|        err_text = _read_stream(getattr(proc, "stderr", None)).strip()
196|        try:
197|            brep_bytes = sandbox.filesystem.read_bytes(
198|                remote_path=BREP_PATH)
199|            measure_text = sandbox.filesystem.read_text(
200|                remote_path=MEASURE_PATH)
201|        except _missing_file_errors():
202|            detail = err_text or log.strip()
203|            run_error = NO_BREP_PREFIX + (": %s" % detail if detail else "")
204|            return {"brep_bytes": None, "measure": None, "log": log,
205|                    "run_error": run_error}
206|        if len(brep_bytes) > MAX_BREP_BYTES:
207|            raise ValueError(
208|                "BREP is %d bytes (over the %d-byte limit); refusing"
209|                % (len(brep_bytes), MAX_BREP_BYTES))
210|        import json as _json
211|
212|        measure = _json.loads(measure_text)
213|        return {"brep_bytes": brep_bytes, "measure": measure, "log": log,
214|                "run_error": None}
215|    finally:
216|        if own:
217|            try:
218|                sandbox.terminate()
219|            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 -- terminate is best-effort
220|                pass

226|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):
227|    """PASS iff every check holds and the mismatch fraction is within tol.
228|
229|    `check_fails`: failed checks at the baseline yardstick (bbox, volume,
230|    ...); `mismatch`: answer-XOR-reference fraction of reference volume
231|    (None when the shape could not be intersected). Returns
232|    (passed, fails).
233|    """
234|    fails = list(check_fails or [])
235|    if mismatch is None:
236|        fails = fails + ["mismatch error"]
237|    elif mismatch > tol:
238|        fails = fails + ["mismatch %.1f%%" % (100.0 * mismatch)]
239|    return (not fails), fails

247|    mismatch fraction from checks.score; tests pass synthetic values.

262|    """Score built shapes at both tolerances (needs cadquery + checks).
263|
264|    The reference shapes are trusted code (exam jobs.py, the generator);
265|    only model answers must stay out of this process. Returns the
266|    grade_result dict plus "mismatch". `checks` is imported lazily from
267|    the frozen first-test copy.

1|"""Measure a CadQuery result and compare it with a job's expected values (PLAN.md section 6)."""
2|import cadquery as cq
3|
4|TOL_POS = 0.1      # mm, bounding-box faces
5|TOL_COM = 0.3      # mm, centre of mass
6|TOL_REL = 0.01     # 1 %, volume and surface area
7|TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact
8|
9|
10|def to_shape(result):
11|    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
12|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
13|        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
14|    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
15|        return result.toCompound()
16|    return result
17|
18|
19|def measure(result):
20|    s = to_shape(result)
21|    bb = s.BoundingBox()
22|    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
23|    return {
24|        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
25|        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
26|        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
27|        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
28|        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
29|        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
30|    }
31|
32|
33|def compare(m, e):
34|    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
35|    fails = []
36|    if m["solids"] != 1:
37|        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
38|    if not m["valid"]:
39|        fails.append("invalid shape")
40|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
41|        fails.append("bbox")
42|    for k in ("volume", "area"):
43|        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
44|            fails.append(k)
45|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
46|        fails.append("com")
47|    return fails
48|
49|
50|def mismatch(answer, reference):
51|    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
52|    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
53|    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
54|    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
55|    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()
56|
57|
58|def score(answer, reference, expected):
59|    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
60|    m = measure(answer)
61|    fails = compare(m, expected)
62|    try:
63|        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
64|    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
65|        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
66|    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
67|    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
68|        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
69|    return (not fails), fails, m

7|TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact
8|
9|
10|def to_shape(result):
11|    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
12|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
13|        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
14|    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
15|        return result.toCompound()
16|    return result
17|
18|
19|def measure(result):
20|    s = to_shape(result)
21|    bb = s.BoundingBox()
22|    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
23|    return {
24|        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
25|        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
26|        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
27|        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
28|        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
29|        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
30|    }
31|
32|
33|def compare(m, e):
34|    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
35|    fails = []
36|    if m["solids"] != 1:
37|        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
38|    if not m["valid"]:
39|        fails.append("invalid shape")
40|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
41|        fails.append("bbox")
42|    for k in ("volume", "area"):
43|        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
44|            fails.append(k)
45|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
46|        fails.append("com")
47|    return fails
48|
49|
50|def mismatch(answer, reference):
51|    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
52|    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
53|    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
54|    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
55|    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()
56|
57|
58|def score(answer, reference, expected):
59|    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
60|    m = measure(answer)
61|    fails = compare(m, expected)
62|    try:
63|        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
64|    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
65|        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
66|    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
67|    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
68|        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
69|    return (not fails), fails, m

+    F10 rim ring), so those lines count as cutter positions too."""

p = generator.first_params(10)

old_rim_fuse = 's = s.fuse(_zcyl((%s)/2, 0, 0, %s, (%s + %s)))' % (generator.num(c['Dout']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['rh']))
old_rim_cut = 's = s.cut(_zcyl((%s)/2, 0, 0, (%s - 1), ((%s + %s) + 1)))' % (generator.num(c['Din']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['rh']))
new_rim_fuse = 'rim = _zcyl((%s)/2, 0, 0, %s, (%s + %s))' % (generator.num(c['Dout']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['rh']))
new_rim_cut = 'rim = rim.cut(_zcyl((%s)/2, 0, 0, %s, ((%s + %s) + 1)))' % (generator.num(c['Din']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['H']), generator.num(c['rh']))
assert new_rim_fuse in new and new_rim_cut in new
old = new.replace(new_rim_fuse, old_rim_fuse).replace(new_rim_cut, old_rim_cut).replace('s = s.fuse(rim)', 's = s')
for label, src in (('new', new), ('old', old)):
    ref = generator.build_source(src)
    H = c['H']; Rb, Rt = c['Db']/2, c['Dt']/2; rrb, rrt = c['Drb']/2, c['Drt']/2; tf = c['tf']
    R0 = Rb + (Rt-Rb)*(H-1)/H
    vb = math.pi/3*(R0**2+R0*Rt+Rt**2)
    r0 = rrb + (rrt-rrb)*(H-1-tf)/(H+1-tf); r1 = rrb + (rrt-rrb)*(H-tf)/(H+1-tf)
    vr = math.pi/3*(r0**2+r0*r1+r1**2)
    slab = cq.Solid.makeBox(200,200,1, cq.Vector(-100,-100,H-1))
    got = ref.intersect(slab).Volume()
    print(label, 'slab=', round(got,3), 'analytic=', round(vb-vr,3), 'rel-err=', abs(got-(vb-vr))/abs(vb-vr))
